//: Repo-level settings that must be identical across all seven packages. Snapshotted from tselect-npm/url with `tselect pull`. Keys map one-to-one onto PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}, except `security` — see below.
//merge: Squash is the only merge method, matching `allowed_merge_methods: ["squash"]` in rulesets/pr-required.json. Leaving merge/rebase enabled in settings while the ruleset rejects them just produces buttons that fail at click time. PR_TITLE + BLANK because a squashed branch's gitmoji series collapses into one commit and the release workflow reads the emoji off the PR title.
//features: Issues stay on — the modernization tracks findings there. Wiki and Projects are on because that is the reference repo's state; Discussions stay off.
//actions: Its own endpoint (PUT …/actions/permissions), not part of the PATCH body. Worth managing because the failure is silent: `status-code` had Actions switched off entirely, so its CI would never have run and CodeQL default setup could not be enabled either — nothing reports that, the workflows simply never start.
//security: Not part of the PATCH body — each of these is its own REST endpoint, applied by the `security` provider. Grouped here so one file is the whole desired state for a repo.

security.//code_scanning: CodeQL default setup. `actions` is in the language list on the reference repo and is the one worth keeping — the shared workflows are the largest attack surface here. Weekly, default query suite.
